item.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless edge inference enables Physical-AI devices to execute edge-inferred actions using transmitted sensory inputs. Since the risk of incorrect actions vary across observations and tasks, the associated uplink transmission of sensory inputs requires different levels of wireless reliability. For instance, applying a fixed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirement can overprovision low-risk tasks while underprovisioning high-risk ones. Therefore, we propose risk-aware control for edge inference (RACE), which maps predicted action-failure probability and task criticality to adaptive SINR targets and combines them with deadline-derived SINR requirements. A slow-timescale large language model (LLM) proposes task requirements for deterministic validation, while a fast hybrid actor selects inference configurations and transmit power levels, complemented by analytical receive beamforming and finite power restoration. Simulations show $11\%$ improvement in the average accuracy-latency-energy objective over fixed-high-SINR control, with near-zero constraint outage.
item.dc:creator: Amin Farajzadeh, Melike Erol-Kantarci

item.title: Janus: One Agent, Two Roles for Digital Twin Construction and Network Orchestration
item.description: arXiv:2611.14920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are increasingly large-scale, heterogeneous, and dynamic, posing significant challenges to network modeling and control. Digital twins offer a promising solution, but existing approaches typically rely on static models and decouple twin construction from network orchestration, limiting adaptability. Meanwhile, large language models (LLMs) provide strong reasoning capabilities but struggle with graph-structured data and are highly sensitive to prompt design, making inference unreliable. In this paper, we propose Janus, an agentic LLM-based framework that unifies digital twin construction and network orchestration within a closed-loop system. At the core of Janus is a novel NetTwin agent, which introduces a new one-agent, two-role paradigm, enabling a single agent to simultaneously construct the digital twin from partial observations while performing task-driven network decision-making. To realize this, we design a modular architecture with three functional roles, including planner, modeler, and coder, along with a newly designed unified prompt module that further enhances graph reasoning robustness. Extensive evaluations on wireless networks with up to 200 nodes and two representative tasks, including user association and SAGIN routing, show that Janus achieves over 90% digital twin accuracy and near-optimal performance with gaps within 10.53%, while maintaining moderate computational overhead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability of Janus, paving the way for AI-native autonomous wireless network orchestration.
item.dc:creator: Peijun Hou, Yue Zhang, Yi Wei, Nan Cen

item.title: CommJEPA: When Predictive Representation Learning Meets Wireless Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2611.14961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an integral part of wireless systems, yet much of today's wireless AI remains task-specific and reactive, with models typically trained to map current observations to predefined outputs or reconstruct observed data. While effective for individual tasks, such approaches provide limited support for learning what is predictable, reusable, and transferable in dynamic wireless environments. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) offers a different perspective by learning predictive representations in latent space that capture informative structure in the observations. In this article, we introduce Communication JEPA (CommJEPA) as a communication-oriented framework for predictive representation learning. The central idea is bidirectional. JEPA can equip wireless systems with predictive representations for capturing latent channel and environmental dynamics, integrating heterogeneous observations, adapting to changing conditions, and supporting future decisions. Conversely, the physical structure, partial observability, multiple time scales, action-dependent evolution, and resource constraints of wireless systems motivate new communication-aware JEPA designs. We develop this mutual perspective, organize the resulting design space, and discuss representative JEPA-based wireless instantiations for prediction and control. We further highlight open challenges toward scalable, interactive, and predictive wireless intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Feiran You, Hongyang Du, Kang Wei, Jun Li, Abbas Jamalipour

item.title: Priority-Based Network Access with Strict-Priority Scheduling in PLCA Multidrop Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.15281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shared-medium Ethernet is gaining renewed attention across industrial domains, driven by the adoption of 10BASE-T1S. In such multidrop networks, collision-free and deterministic medium access is achieved through Physical Layer Collision Avoidance (PLCA). However, PLCA follows a node-based cyclic access structure that does not account for traffic priority, leading to high access latency for time-sensitive traffic and limited scalability with increasing network size. Existing PLCA extensions improve latency for selected devices but remain restricted to node-based access and do not support network-wide traffic differentiation. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a priority-based network access and scheduling mechanism for multidrop networks. The proposed approach decouples medium access from node-based ordering and enables class-based prioritization, allowing high-priority traffic from any device to be transmitted ahead of lower-priority traffic. It further supports a configuration that emulates Strict Priority (SP) scheduling, providing low and bounded access latency for highest-priority traffic. Analytical bounds on the worst-case access latency are derived, validated, and shown to be tight. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed mechanism reduces the maximum observed access latency for high-priority traffic by over 65% compared to PLCA, with latency increasing by less than 1% as the network grows from 8 to 40 devices.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elattar, Zhe Lou, Georg Carle

item.title: When Cause Attribution Is Not Enough: Action-Value Control for Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with Discrete Encoder Switching
item.description: arXiv:2611.15513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A task-oriented semantic communication receiver that selects among independently trained encoders must answer two questions when performance degrades: which component is responsible, and which available action best restores task performance. These are distinct decision problems. Under discrete encoder switching, correctly identifying the dominant information-loss component does not necessarily identify the action that most reduces task error. Diagnosis and intervention should therefore be treated as separate problems. We support this finding with two complementary instruments. The first is a receiver-side diagnostic that partitions task-information loss into encoder and channel components and supplies population-valid task-error bounds conditional on one-sided information estimators. The second is an offline-supervised, online label-free action-value controller built from two monotone (isotonic) maps that target a reduction in measured error. The main experiments focus on two complementary axis-aligned actions that cleanly isolate the effect of discrete switching; a pilot further examines a combined action. Evaluation covers a controlled model with closed-form ground truth, three DeepJSCC vision systems, and a non-vision pilot. On STL-10, the diagnosis correctly identifies the larger loss component at 80% of operating points, yet matches the oracle-best action only 25% of the time. Structural mismatch caps any diagnosis-driven loss-ordering policy at 46% accuracy, even with perfect knowledge of the ordering. The action-value controller, which exploits the magnitude of each loss deficit, achieves 0.86, compared to 0.28 for the raw rule. Where the encoder is rarely the bottleneck, the controller naturally retains the physical-layer default, yielding robust and selective intervention.
item.dc:creator: Moirangthem Tiken Singh

item.title: Orthogonal Code-Based Parallel Signaling for PLCA in Shared-Medium Ethernet
item.description: arXiv:2611.15577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical Layer Collision Avoidance (PLCA) enables collision-free channel access in shared-medium Ethernet by granting each node an exclusive transmission opportunity (TO) in a sequential, cyclic manner. This sequential, node-based access structure, however, is the root cause of PLCA's fundamental limitations, causing access latency to grow with network size and idle TOs to accumulate when traffic is sparse, a limitation inherited by existing PLCA extensions. To address this, we propose OC-PLCA, an orthogonal code-based parallel signaling mechanism for PLCA. Rather than signaling sequentially, all nodes with pending traffic transmit their unique Walsh-Hadamard code simultaneously to signal their intent to transmit. Since these codes are mutually orthogonal, each node independently identifies the complete set of active nodes, allowing the transmission cycle to include only active nodes and eliminating idle TOs entirely. We further investigate the impact of quantization on active node detection, and propose a grouping-based extension that preserves unambiguous detection for networks of an arbitrary number of nodes. Theoretical analysis shows that OC-PLCA reduces signaling overhead by 88% for an 8-node network, with the reduction growing as network size increases. Simulation results confirm significant reductions in observed access latency across a range of network loads and heterogeneous node activity.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elattar, Ahmed Abdelkader, Zhe Lou, Georg Carle

item.title: From Isolated Protocols to Integrated Pipelines: Benchmarking IoT Communication in the MASA Living Lab
item.description: arXiv:2611.15595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of real-time IoT communication systems depends not only on individual transport protocols, serialization formats, and data-processing stages, but also on how these components interact within the complete communication pipeline. Selecting an appropriate communication stack is therefore application-dependent and requires considering processing capabilities, network characteristics, communication patterns, and reliability requirements. This paper provides an experimental, evidence-based analysis of these interactions through a controlled benchmark of integrated communication pipelines deployed in the MASA living lab. We jointly evaluate local processing overhead, end-to-end latency, jitter, throughput, and delivery reliability across different combinations of transport, messaging, serialization, and compression mechanisms. Results show that component-level processing costs do not directly predict end-to-end performance. In particular, differences of only tens of microseconds in serialization or compression costs can coexist with several-millisecond differences in end-to-end latency, while middleware buffering and transport behavior substantially affect timing performance. The results demonstrate that communication-stack components should be evaluated as integrated pipelines and under representative operating loads rather than ranked independently.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Solida, Enrico Rossini, Marcello Pietri, Marco Picone, Carlo Augusto Grazia

item.title: Quota-Based Traffic Classification for Bounded Jitter in Multi-CQF under Redundancy Mechanisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.15622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The demand for deterministic and reliable communication is rapidly increasing in industrial networks. Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) addresses these requirements through deterministic scheduling and redundancy mechanisms such as Multiple Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (Multi-CQF) and Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER). Multi-CQF guarantees bounded end-to-end (E2E) latency and jitter, while FRER provides seamless fault tolerance through redundant forwarding. With static traffic classification, redundant paths with different hop counts can exhibit different E2E latency ranges. This can amplify jitter when a failure causes packets to be delivered over a longer redundant path. To address this, we propose a quota-based traffic classification mechanism that adapts class assignments hop-by-hop using a common E2E latency budget derived from the primary path, thereby mitigating jitter amplification. Simulation results show that the proposed mechanism reduces jitter amplification by up to 70% and latency degradation by up to 41% compared to static classification.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elattar, Zhe Lou, Georg Carle

item.title: Energy Aware Optimization of Non-Deterministic Task-Based Intermittent Computing Nodes with Thimble
item.description: arXiv:2611.15681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intermittent computing nodes run on harvested energy, which they store in capacitors and spend in short bursts of computation. Choosing those capacitors is a trade-off: large capacitors can power large tasks but leak more current, wasting harvested energy, while small capacitors leak less but cannot power large tasks. Recent work, LEACS, showed that selecting capacitors and mapping tasks to them at compile time improves inference throughput. However, LEACS optimizes the mapping for a predetermined workload, whereas sensor nodes often run data-dependent workloads in which the next task depends on the outcome of earlier ones. We present Thimble, an energy storage system that maps a node's tasks to capacitors at runtime. Thimble models the workload as a Markov chain over tasks and assigns each task to a capacitor by weighing capacitor leakage, the task's energy demand and, when it replans, the likelihood of each future task. We compare Thimble against a reimplementation of LEACS, which ranks every static plan by simulation. When the training trace resembles deployment, Thimble's single design-time solve comes within 0.3--4% of LEACS's throughput. When the deployment conditions drift from the characteristics of the training set, LEACS's throughput-focused static plans can fail sharply. On the lowest-power source we consider, LEACS's plan stalls on deployment traces that harvest less than its training trace, and on some never wakes; Thimble avoids this, with 22--29% higher throughput at the reference workload. A sensitivity sweep over 25 workload profiles on that source shows that Thimble with depth replanning leads LEACS by 22--42% throughout, and what run-time remapping adds: replanning at a fixed interval matches or improves on the static map at 21 of 25 points, by up to 7%.
item.dc:creator: John Madden, Morgan Masters, Alec Levy, Steve McGuire, Colleen Josephson

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Spectrum Data Obfuscation in Next-Generation Spectrum Coexistence Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.15770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In spectrum coexistence systems, the primary user (PU) activity must be partially disclosed for interference avoidance and coordination, while the exact spectrum occupancy information is often restricted due to security and regulatory constraints. To this end, subset-based disclosures can be employed in which the true frequency is included while ambiguity is introduced. This paper shows that naive randomized subset disclosures remain highly vulnerable to information leakage through inference, as temporal structure can be exploited to recover spectrum usage information. Under Markovian dynamics of the PU's spectrum usage, hidden Markov model (HMM) filtering with online learning is applied, while under periodic dynamics, period and phase estimations with phase-aligned statistics are used for inference. To address this vulnerability, structure-aware obfuscation strategies are introduced. For Markovian dynamics, history-based and belief-based schemes are designed to induce model mismatch and limit posterior concentration, while for periodic dynamics, cycle-dominance and decoy-based schemes are designed to manipulate phase-wise statistics and bias the inference process. These obfuscation schemes significantly hinder inference of spectrum information and offer principled disclosure solutions for spectrum coexistence systems.
item.dc:creator: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Sastry Kompella, Joseph A. Molnar

item.title: On Multi-Constrained Path Finding utilizing Grover Search and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.15794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding a path whose totals under several additive metrics all fall inside prescribed ranges is weakly NP-complete. We ask what two quantum algorithms can do for it, against strong classical baselines. For directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) we give a Grover search whose state preparation builds the uniform superposition over all source-to-destination paths with one qubit per arc and no ancilla. We prove it correct, give its exact gate count, and show that measured strings form an error- detecting code whose distance is a girth-like graph parameter. We complete the oracle and count its gates: one search on our largest instance, 136 arc qubits and 262,144 paths, needs about 4.4 x 10^5 Toffoli gates, while classical dynamic programming decides the same instance with 18,754 labels. Grover search needs O(sqrt(N/M)) oracle calls for M good paths among N . Classical meet-in-the-middle matches this exponent in the worst case, and known quantum algorithms with quantum memory beat it. For a staged fabric with node-independent linear weights, maximizing the number of satisfied metrics is max-LINSAT, and with power- of-index weights it is Optimal Polynomial Intersection, where no known polynomial-time classical algorithm matches decoded quantum interferometry (DQI). We verify this translation in simulation and run two small binary instances on IBM Heron processors, which keep 67 % and 15 % of the ideal gain over uniform sampling.
item.dc:creator: Dmitrii Chemodanov

item.title: Machine Learning for Scalable Multi-AP Coordination in IEEE 802.11bn Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Wi-Fi deployments become denser, fully distributed random channel access no longer guarantees the required quality of service. The multi-access point coordination (MAPC) framework introduced in IEEE~802.11bn lets neighboring access points (APs) cooperate, but choosing which APs transmit together and how to configure them remains an open, computationally hard problem. We develop and validate a stack of machine learning (ML) coordination methods, progressing from lightweight hierarchical multi-armed bandits (H-MABs) to a generative pipeline built on graph neural networks (GNNs) and flow matching (FM). The methods are evaluated in simulation and on a hardware testbed, improving throughput over legacy access and scaling coordination to dozens of APs where analytical and search-based methods become intractable.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: The 28th International Conference on Modeling, Analysis and Simulation of Wireless and Mobile Systems (MSWiM 2026)
item.dc:creator: Maksymilian Wojnar, Szymon Szott

item.title: A Connectionless Interaction Model for Network Spatial Proximity Services
item.description: arXiv:2611.16737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a connectionless interaction model for network spatial proximity services. In the network spatial proximity model, the reception of an identification or discovery frame of a nearby wireless node confirms proximity and delivers content at the same time. Current Bluetooth and Wi-Fi specifications and mobile platforms extend this one-way announcement with responses, addressed messages, scheduled group exchange, and relaying, which still do not require a connection. The proposed model describes such interaction independently of a concrete wireless technology. It is based on the roles of nearby nodes, the proximity message as the unit of interaction, twelve pattern properties, and six interaction patterns: announcement, mutual announcement, query-response, addressed exchange, scheduled group exchange, and relay. An exit rule defines when a service should move to a connection-based channel. We analyze how the patterns can be implemented on Android and iOS smartphones through native mechanisms, substitution, composition, embedded bridges, or a step-up to a connection, and we propose a pattern selection method for developers. The model generalizes the earlier network spatial proximity model and refines the interaction primitives of the proximity core. It is illustrated by existing services and systems and supported by published measurements and first-order estimates.
item.dc:creator: Artem Makarov, Dmitry Namiot

item.title: Agentic Orchestration for SLA-Constrained Network Slicing in Programmable Mobile Data Planes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Specification 23.501 (Release 17) defines Maximum Bit Rate (MBR) enforcement at the User Plane Function (UPF) in fifth-generation (5G) networks. Supporting differentiated service-level agreements across the radio access and core networks requires the UPF to enforce MBR limits according to configured slice priorities. During overload, the challenge is to adapt these limits while preserving that differentiation and avoiding oscillations. Building on programmable enforcement and intelligent orchestration, we propose an agentic control loop combining UPF telemetry with locally hosted Large Language Model (LLM) selection from a finite set of admissible rate candidates. Deterministic logic validates each selection and derives Packet Forwarding Control Protocol (PFCP) updates. The evaluated runs show no oscillations or fallbacks and unchanged highest-priority rate limits. These observations establish configuration preservation; delivered per-class QoS protection remains unmeasured.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Moreira, Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Joberto S. B. Martins, Tereza C. Carvalho, Fl\'avio de Oliveira Silva

item.title: Topology-Aware Handover Management for Service Continuity in LEO Satellite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are expected to play a key role in sixth-generation (6G) non-terrestrial networks. The high mobility of LEO satellites necessitates frequent handovers (HOs), posing challenges to service continuity and availability for user equipment. Conventional methods based on handover margin (HOM) and time-to-trigger (TTT) have limited adaptability to time-varying channel conditions and do not explicitly account for the impact of feeder-link and ground station (GS) connectivity on HO interruption time. To address these limitations, this paper develops a topology-aware HO framework based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). The framework uses reference signal received power (RSRP), satellite--GS associations, remaining visibility time, and elevation angles to determine when to initiate an HO and which satellite to select. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed policy achieves a service availability of 99.32% at a minimum elevation angle of 40 degrees, exceeding that of optimized HOM--TTT (O-HT) and least-delay (LD) satellite selection by 1.67 and 1.41 percentage points, respectively. The policy maintains service availability above 97.52% as the minimum elevation angle increases to 55 degrees, demonstrating its ability to sustain high service availability under stricter elevation constraints.
item.dc:creator: Jui-Che Han, Nasir Khan, Siva Satya Sri Ganesh Seeram, Cicek Cavdar

item.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
item.description: arXiv:2611.16879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-RAN distributes network control across multiple autonomous agents, namely xApps and rApps operating over shared radio resources. When an alert or degradation appears, operators currently lack a structured way to trace which decision caused it, what context triggered that decision, and how other agents interacted. Existing explainability tools focus on single-model feature attribution or linear event logging, neither of which captures cross-agent decision chains. We propose the Context Graph, a heterogeneous directed graph that organizes policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer. Its foundational primitive is the Decision-Event node acting as a causal junction, where incoming edges capture triggering context and outgoing edges track downstream consequences that are progressively upgraded through counterfactual verification. Instantiated over existing E2, A1, and O1 data flows, our proof-of-concept demonstrates that compliance and diagnosis queries are resolved at sub-millisecond latency over graphs of tens of thousands of nodes, while reliably distinguishing true causal impacts from spurious correlations.
item.dc:creator: Xijun Wang, Zhaoyang Liu, Xiang Chen, Howard H. Yang, Chenyuan Feng

item.title: Collision-Resilient All-to-All Broadcast Scheduling in Underwater Acoustic Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies all-to-all broadcast scheduling for underwater swarms with collision-resilient physical layers that can decode asynchronously overlapping packets. Propagation-aware collision-free schedulers coordinate packet arrivals but do not account for this reception capability. We first design a data-driven neural reception model that captures per-interferer power and timing effects. The model improves prediction accuracy over SINR baselines while admitting an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The resulting neural-network-embedded MILP (NN-MILP) optimizes transmission times while explicitly encoding schedule-dependent overlaps and the predictor's inference, enabling globally optimal scheduling for small-scale instances. For larger networks, a two-stage ant colony optimization (ACO) heuristic combines low-cost transmission-order search with neural-aware timing refinement. Simulation results show that ACO shortens broadcast rounds compared with existing schedulers. It approaches the NN-MILP optimum on small-scale instances while supporting larger networks at substantially lower computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Guoliang Weng, Enqi Zhang, Lizhao You, Deqing Wang, Liqun Fu

item.title: obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation
item.description: arXiv:2611.15019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Encrypted tunnels are widely used to circumvent censorship, which has drawn censors' efforts to detect and block them. As the circumvention tunnels in widest use have largely converged on TLS, detection has shifted from the content of their traffic to its shape, where recent research and real-world blocking events have revealed exploitable fingerprints of tunneling. Existing traffic-shaping obfuscators such as obfs4, however, are fundamentally limited in hiding these fingerprints, as their application-driven design can only add to the shape that the application creates. A schedule-driven obfuscator, which decides when and how much to send independently of the application, can give tunnels any shape but raises new challenges, first and foremost what a good shape is. This paper presents obfsgen, a schedule-driven obfuscator for tunneling traffic. obfsgen samples its schedule from a generative sequence model of normal traffic, which predicts the future shape of a flow from its whole history, to capture the long-range dependencies that make a flow's shape normal. Built around this model, obfsgen addresses system problems that such an obfuscator faces in practice, such as synchronization across a noisy network. We evaluate the (in)distinguishability that obfsgen offers, the performance overhead that it adds and the computational resources that it requires. We see the schedule-driven architecture as the next generation of tunnel obfuscators, and we hope that obfsgen and the rationale behind its design help make such obfuscators practical and deployable.
item.dc:creator: Kaidong Wu, Wentao Du, Shinan Liu, Diwen Xue

item.title: Rateless Coding for Efficient Model Broadcast in Federated Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.15499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model broadcast in federated learning (FL) with wireless channels faces significant challenges due to large model sizes and heterogeneous, unreliable channel conditions. While rateless coding has been widely adopted in modern broadcast communications to handle channel heterogeneity, its potential for model broadcast in FL remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose a joint source-channel coding scheme based on rateless coding to improve the robustness and efficiency of downlink model broadcast in FL. Specifically, we establish a rigorous convergence analysis of FL to inform the rateless code and quantization design under noisy downlink channel conditions. Moreover, by observing that the iterative process of FL naturally provides prior information about client updates, we leverage client-side local models as conditional prior information to aid the decoding process, thereby reducing transmission costs. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our rateless coding scheme significantly enhances downlink model broadcast efficiency in FL, while retaining comparable training accuracies for both homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions.
item.dc:creator: Zijun Qin, Zuolin Jin, Jingxuan Huang, Ming Xiao, Xianhao Chen

item.title: What Does It Cost to Force-Close a Lightning Channel? Evidence from 974,000 Channel Closes, 2018-2026
item.description: arXiv:2611.16311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bitcoin's Lightning payment network returns the funds of a channel that cannot close cooperatively through pre-signed transactions whose fees and delays fall on its operators. That fee design is being replaced: Bitcoin Core 31.0 removed the mempool rule anchor channels relied on, and the Lightning specification adopted zero-fee commitments in May 2026. What the old design costs has never been measured across fee regimes. We trace every public channel close and every force close on-chain from January 2018 to October 2026, 973,581 closes, and follow each output to its spend. A separate chain index confirms all 698,476 public closes we could compare. Fee spikes did not bring a wave of force closes. Force closes in a spike week and the next were 0.97 times the four weeks before, against 1.02 after ordinary weeks of the same years. A force close costs 2-6 times a cooperative close in fees and locks the closer's balance for days, which outweighs the fees only in low-fee years. When fees are high, pending payments are exposed: in 2023, 18.2% of HTLC timeouts confirmed more than 40 blocks after expiry. Yet since 2021, forwarding nodes lost only 38 payments, each with the preimage already on-chain. Anchor outputs cut late timeouts in fee spikes (20.6% against 30.5%), yet owners rarely bump commitments with them, and miners take most of what third parties sweep. Zero-fee commitments would save only 12% of the anchor mechanism's block space; they should be judged by how promptly payments resolve when fees spike.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Kumar

item.title: Sustainable Federated Fine-Tuning with LoRA: Environmental Impact and Performance Footprint
item.description: arXiv:2611.16856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) enables efficient adaptation of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet its energy and carbon costs across hardware remain poorly understood. We evaluated federated Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning on NVIDIA A40, RTX 6000 Ada, and A100 GPUs using a $2^2$ full factorial design with 135M/360M models and 10/100 local steps. CodeCarbon tracked energy and estimated CO$_2$-equivalent emissions. Descriptive allocation of variation assigned 84.8-91.2% of energy and emissions variation to local steps within these ranges. On A40 and RTX 6000 Ada, configurations with fewer steps achieved comparable accuracy with roughly 6-8-fold lower energy consumption and higher accuracy per kWh. These findings support smaller local budgets for energy-efficient federated fine-tuning within the evaluated setting.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Augusto Londe Ribeiro, Rodrigo Moreira, Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Joberto S. B. Martins, Tereza C. Carvalho, Fl\'avio de Oliveira Silva

item.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2611.17097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference at datacenter scale is fundamentally bottlenecked by memory capacity and bandwidth limits. Because model weights are read-only and identical across instances, conventional architectures that replicate these parameters across the local DRAM of tens of thousands of accelerators incur massive capital expenditures, significant static power dissipation, and redundant memory-fetch energy. A recent proposal to use optical fiber loops as delay-line memory alleviates these issues, but its recirculating loop must hold the whole model: loop length grows with model size, slack is fixed when the ring is built, and the layouts that serve modern Mixture of Experts (MoE) models efficiently do not fit in it. We propose Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), an open-ended hierarchical Tap-and-Amplify fiber architecture that generalizes and replaces the optical ring paradigm. A centralized memory server continuously broadcasts weights to distributed inference nodes that passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics, delivering parameters directly to compute units without intermediate buffering. To overcome the limitations of continuous weight streaming, we use dynamically-sized slack to accommodate large and variable context lengths. We show how removing the restrictions of the optical ring allows OBM to efficiently serve MoE models. Evaluated at a datacenter scale of 80,000 accelerators, OBM eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Atmer, Yuan Yao, Thiemo Voigt, Stefanos Kaxiras

item.title: Versatile yet Efficient Network Traffic Analysis: Offloading Network Foundation Model to SmartNIC
item.description: arXiv:2508.02001v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pervasive encryption makes large-scale labeling infeasible for traffic analysis, while security operations demand edge analysis to avert service degradation and vulnerabilities. These pressures have produced two research lines that advance 1) versatile analysis, via network foundation models for low label dependency, and 2) efficient analysis, via hardware offloading for low analysis latency. However, co-achieving versatility and efficiency via such lines has appeared incompatible, with prior work advancing one while compromising the other, yet we show that this incompatibility is a consequence of polarized design choices across the three components of traffic analysis systems, i.e., traffic processing, model architecture, and analysis execution. In response, we present Nepco, a versatile yet efficient network traffic analysis system that offloads network foundation models to SmartNIC. Our key observation is that discriminative traffic information often exhibits localized patterns within byte sequences, motivating versatile yet efficient localized byte-sequence modeling. To exploit this without incurring the latency bottlenecks of complex encoding steps, we employ a hardware-friendly processing strategy that directly embeds raw byte sequences. To maintain versatility across diverse tasks characterized by spatially shifting features, we explore an observation-driven convolution architecture equipped with hardware-friendly scoring and gating designs. By exploiting translation invariance, this design dynamically locates and extracts salient semantic signatures irrespective of their byte-level offsets. We prototype Nepco on the NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC with multi-engine collaborative analysis execution. The experimental results demonstrate that Nepco achieves macro F1 competitive with the best performances achieved by 8 state-of-the-art network foundation models...
item.dc:creator: Chungang Lin, Xuying Meng, Tianyu Zuo, Weiyao Zhang, Meng Shen, Ruijie Zhao, Guanming Che, Ruiqi Meng, Ziyue Huang, Haitong Luo, Zhiwei Xu, Yujun Zhang

item.title: Contract-Theoretic Semantic Abstraction for Covert Communication in LAENets
item.description: arXiv:2603.01478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Low-Altitude Economy Networks (LAENets), Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) transmit task-related information to the Base Station (BS) under stringent low-probability-of-detection constraints. These constraints limit transmission resources, hindering reliable information delivery through conventional bit-level communication. Semantic Communication (SemCom) addresses this challenge by prioritizing task-relevant information over bit-level accuracy. However, semantic abstraction must balance information loss and redundancy to preserve task reliability and transmission efficiency. Moreover, the BS cannot directly observe or reliably verify UAVs' semantic processing capabilities and abstraction-dependent transmission costs, leading to information asymmetry. We propose an incentive-aware semantic abstraction framework for covert communications in LAENets. Specifically, we adjust UAV-side semantic abstraction levels to provide differentiated covert semantic services under fixed-dimensional transmission payloads. To address information asymmetry, we develop a contract-theoretic model and adopt Prospect Theory (PT) to capture risk-sensitive semantic abstraction decisions under uncertainty. We further design a Regularized Diffusion-based Soft Actor-Critic (RDSAC) algorithm for optimal contract design under PT, incorporating diffusion entropy and action entropy regularization. Numerical results validate the proposed framework and show that RDSAC improves average rewards by 6.77% over SAC and 31.78% over proximal policy optimization.
item.dc:creator: Yansheng Liu, Jinbo Wen, Kun Zhu, Hui Li, Yang Zhang, Jiawen Kang

item.title: Lightweight GenAI for Network Traffic Generation: Fidelity, Augmentation, and Classification
item.description: arXiv:2603.25507v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Network Traffic Classification (NTC) increasingly relies on data-driven models, yet its practical deployment is often constrained by limited labeled data, strict privacy requirements, and the cost of collecting representative traffic traces. While Network Traffic Generation (NTG) provides an effective means to mitigate data scarcity, conventional generative methods struggle to model the complex temporal dynamics of modern traffic and often incur high computational costs. In this article, we investigate lightweight Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) architectures for practical NTG. Rather than generating raw packet bytes or relying on large foundation models, we synthesize compact flow-level traffic representations derived from early packet-header information, enabling transformer-based, state-space, and diffusion models with only a few million parameters. We present a modular GenAI pipeline for NTG and evaluate it along four complementary axes: (i) synthetic traffic fidelity, (ii) synthetic-only training for reduced raw-data sharing in NTC, (iii) data augmentation under low-data regimes, and (iv) computational efficiency. Experiments on two heterogeneous datasets show that lightweight transformer-based and state-space models preserve both static and temporal traffic characteristics, while providing useful synthetic data for downstream NTC. Among them, transformer-based models offer the best fidelity-efficiency trade-off, combining high-quality traffic generation with moderate computational overhead.
item.dc:creator: Giampaolo Bovenzi, Domenico Ciuonzo, Jonatan Krolikowski, Antonio Montieri, Alfredo Nascita, Antonio Pescap\`e, Dario Rossi

item.title: When Does Blockwise Additivity Break? Diagnosing and Repairing the Additive Assumption in Distillation-Based Architecture Search
item.description: arXiv:2611.07487v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Blockwise distillation methods for architecture search, such as DNA, DONNA, LANA and Puzzle, score each candidate replacement block in isolation and combine the scores additively. We ask at which budgets this additivity assumption fails, whether fine-tuning repairs the failure, what diagnoses it, and how it can be repaired cheaply. On DeiT-S, DeiT-B, Swin-T and Qwen2.5-0.5B with seven latency budgets each, an additive integer program trails a pairwise interaction-aware program after fine-tuning by at most 1.6 top-1 points on ImageNet-1k at the mildest budgets, but by up to 17.5 points, and a factor of 1.9 in perplexity, at aggressive ones. After 10,000 fine-tuning steps 3.3-9.9 points remain on DeiT, whereas on Swin-T the gap shrinks to at most about 1.8 points within 500 steps. In a learning-rate sweep with the standard 2,000 steps, 6.0-10.7 points remain on DeiT when each method's rate is chosen by its evaluation-set accuracy. An intervention that keeps the block library and only forbids more than two removals in any three adjacent layers shrinks the DeiT gap from 5.8-17.5 to 0.7-5.2 points, mostly by improving the additive solution: adjacent removals are a major failure pattern. Splitting the additivity error into a metric and a functional part, relative to additive logit changes, indicates where a cheap logit-sum predictor can be trusted. A hybrid search that ranks moves with this predictor and measures only the best needs no pair measurements and, after Holm adjustment, is significantly better than the pairwise program in 10 of 14 ImageNet-1k settings, with no statistically significant losses. An ablation shows that its ranking helps except at the most aggressive DeiT-B budget, where the predictor misleads and random ranking or ten-times-costlier evolution does better.
item.dc:creator: Yuefeng Xu, Jun Yu
